GitHub's Oct. 15 update adds multi-repository work in one Slack or Teams conversation.

WHAT IT DOES
Ask @GitHub to investigate a bug using frontend and backend code, create a tracking issue, or open a pull request for a scoped fix. These are separate steps, not one permission to do everything.

WHY IT MATTERS
Your team's discussion can become actionable work without rebuilding the context in another conversation.

TRY THIS WEEK
In a workspace where @GitHub is installed and authorized, use a sanitized bug thread. Name the owner/repo for frontend and backend. Ask for an investigation with file references and a proposed test. Specify: no edits or pull request yet. Review the findings before requesting a fix.

THE SIGNAL
AI is moving from replies into handoffs. The useful skill is specifying the task, the boundary, and the evidence you need back.

Tech Thursday gave us the same lesson in a different tool: Copilot CLI generated an image batch through MCP, but the host rejected results that missed the standard. More execution still needs a clear acceptance check.

Save this for your next cross-repo bug.
